---
title: "Variables"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

Every variable in the catalogued products, with its definition. Search by
description ("surface temperature", "salinity"), CF standard name, or
variable name. **Datasets** opens the [browser](browse.qmd) filtered to that
variable.

Definitions come from the product's official vocabulary where there is one,
and otherwise from the attributes in the NetCDF files (column *source*):

- **cmip6-cmor-tables**: CMIP6 variables, from the CMIP6 data request
  ([CMOR tables](https://github.com/PCMDI/cmip6-cmor-tables)), per table
  (`Amon`, `Omon`, ...).
- **ecmwf-param-db**: ERA5, from the
  [ECMWF parameter database](https://codes.ecmwf.int/grib/param-db/). The
  catalog's variable is the Copernicus download name (`2m_temperature`); the
  name inside the files is the ECMWF short name (`t2m`).
- **netcdf**: the `long_name`, `standard_name` and `units` attributes in the
  files (20CRv3, GLORYS, BRAN, SODA, HYCOM, ECCO, ...).

Standard names follow the
[CF standard name table](https://cfconventions.org/Data/cf-standard-names/current/build/cf-standard-name-table.html),
the best way to find the same quantity in different products. One product can
use the same standard name at several levels (2 m air temperature and air
temperature on pressure levels are both `air_temperature`), so check the
level or table too.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
vendor = (p) => new URL(`vendor/${p}`, document.baseURI).href
htl = require(vendor("htl/htl.min.js"))
html = htl.html
Inputs = require.alias({"htl@0.3.1/dist/htl.min.js": vendor("htl/htl.min.js")})(
  vendor("@observablehq/inputs/inputs.min.js")
)
variables = FileAttachment("data/variables.json").json()
config = FileAttachment("data/site_config.json").json()
rows = variables.map((v) => ({
  ...v,
  where: v.collection === "cmip6"
    ? `CMIP6 ${v.table_id}`
    : `${v.product}${v.level ? ` (${v.level})` : ""}`,
  // searched only: "-" and "_" as spaces (see browse.qmd)
  text: [v.long_name, v.standard_name, v.description]
    .filter(Boolean).join(" ").replace(/[-_]/g, " "),
  browse: browseUrl(v)
}))
browseUrl = (v) => {
  const p = new URLSearchParams();
  for (const k of ["collection", "product", "table_id", "level", "variable_id"]) {
    if (v[k] != null) p.append(k, v[k]);
  }
  return `browse.html?${p}`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
variables.length === 0
  ? html`<div class="alert alert-warning">The variable list is not available in this build.</div>`
  : html`<span></span>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof found = Inputs.search(rows, {
  placeholder: "e.g. surface temperature",
  label: "Search",
  columns: ["where", "variable_id", "nc_name", "text"],
  width: 380
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table(found, {
  columns: [
    "where", "variable_id", "nc_name", "long_name", "standard_name", "units",
    "description", "source", "browse"
  ],
  header: {
    where: "product / table", variable_id: "variable", nc_name: "in file",
    long_name: "long name", standard_name: "standard name", browse: ""
  },
  format: {
    description: (d) => d == null ? "" : html`<span title=${d}>${d}</span>`,
    source: (d, i, data) => html`<span title=${data[i].source_version ?? ""}>${d ?? "—"}</span>`,
    browse: (d) => html`<a href=${d}>Datasets</a>`
  },
  width: {description: 320, long_name: 240, standard_name: 220},
  rows: 25,
  select: false,
  layout: "auto"
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<p class="small text-body-secondary">The full list (all columns, including
the file each definition was checked against) is
<code>${config.catalog_path.replace(/[^/]*$/, "")}whoi_cmip_vocabulary.csv</code>,
next to the catalogs. See <a href="catalog.html#variables">Catalog</a> for how
to use it with intake-esm.</p>`
```
